question: According to DSM-5, symptoms of ADHD must be present for at least how long, and must have been present before what age?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 3 months is insufficient; the duration criterion is 6 months. The age cut-off shifted from 7 years (DSM-IV) to 12 years in DSM-5.

Correct. DSM-5 requires symptoms to persist for ≥6 months and to have been present before age 12 years in multiple settings. (DSM-IV used age 7; this change acknowledged that ADHD is often not identified until middle school.)
Incorrect. The duration (6 months) is right, but the age-of-onset criterion changed from <7 years (DSM-IV) to <12 years in DSM-5.
Incorrect. The minimum symptom duration is 6 months, not 12 months. 12 years is the correct age-of-onset cut-off.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the DSM-5 ADHD criteria: duration ≥6 months, onset <12 years, impairment in ≥2 settings. Note the change from DSM-IV's age-7 cut-off.
Well done. ADHD requires ≥6 months of symptoms, onset before age 12, in ≥2 settings — these three anchors are the backbone of the diagnostic criteria.
